column1:
The FOMC’s “hawkish hold” at 5.25–5.50% with ongoing balance-sheet runoff is consistent with rule-like policy behavior (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) and forecast-targeting best practice (Svensson and Woodford), given only “modest” recent disinflation and a still-strong labor market (Okun’s law). The explicit commitment not to cut until inflation is “moving sustainably toward 2%” reinforces credibility and mitigates time-inconsistency/inflation-bias concerns highlighted in the literature (Bernanke; inflation-bias models). Operationally, reliance on administered rates (interest on reserves, ON RRP/repo) reflects the post-2008 framework for maintaining control of money-market rates during QT (Federal Reserve/FRBNY). Net tone: slightly positive on progress and “better balanced” risks, but overall cautiously hawkish given the high bar for cuts.
